Situations / Nona Midchain Commission

Nona’s Midchain Commission — Aruhe Survey

The Ask

This is the second thing Nona offers Perrin, not the first. The sewer investigation (Warren — Grung in the Sewers) is the immediate ask at the table. Aruhe comes later, privately, once the meal is done and the Tangle leads have been distributed. She does not mention it to anyone else at the table.

Nona found a reference to Aruhe in forty-year-old Passage route notes — a waypoint entry: good water, good stone, one approach, don’t stay past dark. No explanation of that last line. She cross-checked the chart against three other old sources. Every one describes the same thing: high cliffsides, a single navigable harbour entrance, a deep-water anchorage inside. The island sits east of Karath, inside the reef shadow of the Verdant Teeth, and has been deserted for as long as anyone currently alive can remember.

She chose it specifically because the Grung avoid it. An island Grung patrols will not land on is an island no Crown vessel will find evidence of Grung near. She has worked out that the avoidance creates a blind spot. She has not worked out why the Grung avoid it.

Her exact words to Perrin, paraphrased: the Passage needs a fixed place in the Midchain, not just routes. The Below is an exit; she wants a door that opens both ways. Aruhe might be it. She wants to know if it can be held. She wants Perrin to tell her that, not a report.

She will contact the Uncertainty via signal lantern each evening at dusk. Perrin answers. She asks three questions. He answers in twenty-five words or fewer.

What Nona Does Not Know

DM Note

The Grung call Aruhe

“the island that is already eaten.” They patrol the surrounding reefs but have not landed on it in living memory. The coastal strip is abnormally crowded — too many giant frogs, scorpions, snakes, and spiders packed against the shoreline, pressed there as if something worse holds the interior.

Something does. The Blight has established a Memorial in the abandoned interior. The Death Bloom is at the island’s centre. The corruption has pushed through every flooded ditch and terrace structure outward from the Death Bloom. What is left in the interior is not wilderness — it is a dungeon.

None of this is visible from the sea.

Toy Fields

FieldValue
VerbScouts. Nona sends Perrin ahead of the decision, not after it. What he finds sets the terms — and what he finds is not what she sent him to find.
Unstable ConditionNona believes the island is empty. The Blight believes the same thing about the island. One of them is about to learn otherwise.
ConsequencePositive survey report opens the Tangle’s first real Midchain anchor — if the Blight can be cleared. Honest report gives Nona what she needs to make the real decision.
Link of RelevanceThis is what Nona held back from the table conversation — the work she mentioned to Perrin by name, not to the party. It is the first thing she has given him that is not a favour, a debt, or a test.

Commission Objectives

Nona wants answers to five questions. She does not need them all at once.

#QuestionWhat It Determines
1Is the harbour deep enough for a Tier 2 vessel at high tide?Can the Saltmarsh Trader use it as a base
2Is there freshwater on the island?Settlement viability without resupply infrastructure
3Is the entrance defensible by a small crew?Whether five fighters can hold access during construction
4Is there sign of current occupation or frequent visitation?Whether anything has found the island in the years since the charts were drawn
5What is the Grung patrol frequency and closest approach?Whether the location can remain clandestine for the 18–24 months a shipyard takes

Question 4 is the one that answers itself the moment the party lands.

Daily Check-In — Signal Lantern Protocol

The Uncertainty carries paired signal lanterns: one rail-mounted aft, partner kept below. Range 30 miles, 25-word message limit.

Nona’s format each evening: [Condition check] — [Objective update] — [One question]

The condition check is always first: she wants to know the party is alive before she asks about the island. If there is no reply by two hours past dusk, she waits one more evening.

What Perrin sends back: short, factual, in order. Nona is reading these in the dark. She is not looking for reassurance.

DM Note

If the lantern is destroyed or lost, Nona will not know what happened. The party is operating without a net.

Running the Survey

Three-phase sequence with escalating danger. The party can complete phases 1–2 without triggering the Blight. Phase 3 is the dungeon.

Phase 1 — Approach and Harbour (Safe)

The harbour entrance is technical but navigable. Correct bearing (east-northeast on the old chart) is required; the gap is only visible on direct approach.

TaskCheckDCNotes
Navigate reef entrance, first passDexterity (Water Vehicles)10 / 14With/without bearing note. Failure: grounded on outer reef, 2d6 hull HP damage.
Assess harbour depthIntelligence (Navigation)13Success: reliable depth estimate (~40 ft at centre).
Read the shoreline fauna behaviourWisdom (Perception)12Success: something is pressing the animals outward from the interior. Displacement, not natural crowding.

Inside the harbour: deep water (~40 ft at centre), limestone cliffs on three sides, a narrow shingle beach at the back. The cliffs are 150–200 ft. One stone staircase cut into the cliff face above the beach leads to the plateau.

Phase 2 — Clifftop Survey (Dangerous, Not Blight)

The plateau above the harbour is overgrown. Old stonework — terrace walls and collapsed structures — is visible under the growth. The stonework has been dissolving at the base: acid drainage from the interior has reached the terrace footings.

TaskCheckDCNotes
Assess clifftop defensibilityIntelligence (any military background)10Clear yes — sight lines cover the approach, high ground holds the entrance.
Identify acid drainage sourceIntelligence (Investigation)12Traces toward the interior. PC knows it is coming from inside the island.
Investigate terrace stoneworkWisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Nature)13The terraces dissolved from below, not from neglect. Something in the interior is producing this.
Survey freshwater sourceWisdom (Survival)11A freshwater spring feeds the drainage channel. It runs year-round.
DM Note

The

don’t stay past dark warning. The original Passage runner who wrote this note landed in the harbour, climbed to the plateau, noted the freshwater and the cliff approach, and then heard the interior at dusk. He left. He never elaborated. He also never went back. If the party is on the plateau at dusk and makes a DC 10 Perception check, they hear it too: sound that should be wind moving through the old terrace walls, except the air is still.

Phase 3 — Interior (Blight)

The interior is the dungeon. The Death Bloom is at the centre. The corruption has spread through every flooded ditch and terrace structure. A party that moves inland triggers Blight encounter content.

DM Note

Do not require the party to clear the interior to complete the survey. Phases 1–2 are enough for Nona’s five questions. The interior is a choice — and a loaded one, because the site cannot be used as a settlement while the Blight holds the interior. Perrin will know this when he sees it.

Grung Proximity

Aruhe’s surrounding reefs are part of the Verdant Teeth patrol circuit. The Grung turn back at Aruhe’s beach line — they do not land.

  • Patrol boats: flat-bottomed, 2–3 crew, darts and boarding hooks
  • Circuit frequency: every 36–48 hours past the eastern reef
  • A ship anchored inside the harbour is not visible from the patrol route
  • A ship anchored outside on the approach is visible within 48 hours
  • Any light or fire on the island at night is visible from the Karath side
DM Note

The Grung response to a ship at Aruhe is not a territorial challenge. It is retreat followed by a larger force. They do not want to know what is there. They want whatever is there to stay there.

What Nona Will Do With an Honest Report

She will be quiet for a moment. Then she will ask how bad. Then she will ask if Perrin thinks it can be cleared. She is not asking the party to do it immediately. She is asking if it is possible. The Below gives the Tangle time; this site gives them permanence. She will wait for permanence.

She will not punish an honest assessment. She will punish a report that she later discovers was incomplete.

Outcomes

OutcomeResult
Survey completed, Blight reported honestlyNona takes the full picture to the Tangle. The commission becomes a longer-arc project: clear the island, then build.
Survey completed, Blight omittedNona proceeds. The Tangle sends a construction team. They find out. Nona finds out Perrin knew.
Interior cleared as part of the surveyThe site is viable immediately. Nona’s standing in the Tangle shifts significantly. Perrin’s standing with Nona shifts more.
Party driven off by Blight or GrungPartial information. Nona gets enough to know the site is complicated. She asks Perrin to go back.
Grung discover the operationVerdant Teeth knows someone was at Aruhe. Their response is unusual — not territorial but alarmed. The site is now a political problem, not just a logistical one.

Triggers

  • Perrin agrees to the commission at Nona’s table
  • Nona mentions “the work” she referenced earlier and Perrin follows up
  • The party is departing Calveno and Perrin asks what Nona needs
